messages:
Marta L: Heads up — noticed a bunch of tiny GPU pods getting scattered across eu-west1 racks after the recent repair sweep. Latency tail is up for some inference jobs.
Jason H: ugh, that sounds like the new repair controller's drain scheduling. Do you have example node IDs?
Marta L: yeah pasted a short list from the noisy-scheduler logs:
Marta L: ```
node-ew1-rack3-12 drain start
node-ew1-rack7-04 kernel oops -> cordon
reschedule: pod gpu-small-rl-7 -> node-ew1-rack1-02
reschedule: pod gpu-small-rl-8 -> node-ew1-rack9-01
```
Marta L: the important bit is pods that used to be co-located (same AZ shelf) are now spread, which increases inter-pod NVLink hops for some tiny gangs.
Alex P: is this the repair run that changed the `preferredRackAffinity` scoring? We pushed that change last week to avoid tight hot racks.
Priya S: yes we did, but we also added a fallback that splits gangs when a single shelf can't fit them. could be interacting badly with the tiny-pod binpacker.
Jason H: can we confirm whether these are fractional GPU pods (1/4 or 1/8 slot)? I think the binpacker treats them differently and the repair controller does a best-effort move.
Marta L: they're fractional 0.25 slots mostly. observed more evictions for those in the 02:00-03:00 repair window.
k8s-bot: Notice: drain-runner@ew1 initiated 2026-03-18T02:11Z for 14 nodes (policy: proactive-maintenance)
Alex P: I suspect two compounding things: (1) repair-runner prefers spreading to reduce rack pressure, (2) the fractional binpacker prefers tightly co-locating fractional pods to avoid leftover fragments — they conflict.
Priya S: if repair-runner spreads but binpacker later tries to consolidate, we could end up thrashing and causing evictions. We saw similar in dev where `consolidation-retry` backoff wasn't set.
Jason H: quick mitigation — can we throttle repair-runner concurrency for eu-west1 and bump the consolidation backoff? low-risk and reversible.
Marta L: +1. also we should reject moves that increase NVLink hop count for tiny gangs above threshold. fallback to same-rack only if it doesn't raise hop count.
Alex P: good idea. I can add a soft constraint: prefer same-shelf routing when pods in a gang reference the same gang-id label. fallback still allowed but with higher eviction cost.
Priya S: I'll draft the change and run a small canary in ew1-rackpool A tomorrow morning (0200 window). Also propose adding a repair-runner metric for "gang-hop-incidents" so we can alert before SLO breach.
Jason H: timeline? If canary looks good we can enable to all ew1 racks next week.
Marta L: canary ok for me. Also let's add a kquery alert: if 95th latency for model/vision-large climbs > 200ms above baseline after repair-runner activity -> page oncall.
k8s-bot: Action recorded: ticket #INFRA-9345 created (owner: Alex P) — "repair-runner + binpacker conflict: gang hop reduction + backoff". Can a dev own canary run?
Marta L: I'll own the canary checks and smoke tests. I'll post results in this thread.
Alex P: will push the soft-constraint PR today and link it. thanks.
Priya S: will prepare rollout playbook + alert dashboards.
Jason H: thanks all. If we still see stray evictions after the fix, next step is to add a conservative descheduler window during maintenance runs.
Marta L: noted. I'll follow up with logs and a small before/after table after canary (latency, eviction count, avg hop). :thumbsup:
